text:
lina: Hey 👋 hit a weird auth edge in the sampleapp during onboarding. TL;DR: project-scoped env var REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY is being ignored if REDWOOD_API_KEY present, but SDK should prefer project key per docs. Logs below.

ashley: ugh, saw that. Can you paste the exact env vars and the small repro? Which SDK version?

lina: repro steps:
1) export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-prod-xxx
2) export REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY=sk-project-yyy
3) start sampleapp (node)
Expected: SDK uses project key so requests hit project scope
Observed: outbound auth header shows sk-prod-xxx
Log snippet:
[INFO] auth: resolved key -> sk-prod-xxx
Code snippet in sampleapp:
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY || process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY })

ashley: that code looks inverted — sampleapp has fallback the wrong way. But our SDK's discovery logic (v1.4.2) should enforce project key precedence. Could be packaging bug in sampleapp or bundler replaced env ordering.

raj: I think there's also an issue with dotenv parsing in the sampleapp container image — we strip underscores in the entrypoint step for legacy reasons. Not sure yet.

sam: @lina can you run `npx envinfo` and paste `node -v` + SDK version from package.json? Dev-bot will also post the CI deploy that touched bundling yesterday.

dev-bot: CI: Build #4821 — bumped sampleapp SDK to 1.4.2 in package-lock. No env transform steps recorded in Dockerfile since last deploy.

lina: node v18.16.0, SDK 1.4.2 in node_modules, bundle appears to include our fallback snippet from 1.3.9. Guessing lockfile mismatch.

ashley: ok, next steps: lina — can you change sampleapp to explicit ordering for now and open a tiny PR to fix Dockerfile env passthrough. raj — can you audit the entrypoint script for dotenv transformations. I'll add a short deprecation warning in SDK for ambiguous env vars in 1.4.3.

raj: will do. Also propose adding a runtime warning when both keys present: "Both REDWOOD_API_KEY and REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY set — using REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY" to reduce confusion.

sam: can we also make the SDK hot-rotate streaming connections gracefully? current behavior drops streams when key rotates, causing retries to restart the whole conversation.

ashley: good point — add a ticket to ensure rotation triggers token refresh w/o terminating persistent streams (use 401 handler + soft reconnect). I'll file it.

lina: thanks all — PR incoming for sampleapp + link to repro gist in the PR. :pray:
